description: Cross-session Claude Code recall scenarios. Each step runs as a NEW headless `claude -p` session against the same project + MemContext DB. Labels come from the scenario's intent (what the user decided), written before any run. Value keys map to case-insensitive regexes; the harness wraps each in alnum boundaries (underscore counts as a separator). Kinds: capture/change (user states or changes a decision; DB state is checked after), suggest (assistant proposes an alternative; user's decision must stay current), other (unrelated work), recall (answer scored on its final `CURRENT:` line), act (a file assignment is scored, plus the `CURRENT:` line).

project.name: billing-api
project.description: HTTP service that issues invoices and records payments.

steps.prompt: We've made a call on storage: this service will use PostgreSQL as its database. Please record that decision.
Which database engine does this service use?
Change of plan: we're moving this service's database from PostgreSQL to SQLite to keep deployment simple. Please record the new decision.
Create config/db.py containing a single line DB_ENGINE = "<engine>" with the lowercase name of the database engine we currently use.

project.name: order-events
project.description: Publishes order lifecycle events for downstream consumers.

steps.prompt: Decision: we'll use RabbitMQ as the message broker for publishing order events. Please record it.
We've reconsidered the message broker: switching from RabbitMQ to Kafka for its replay support. Please update the decision.
What message broker are we publishing order events to?
One more change on the broker: Kafka is too heavy for our ops team, so we're going with NATS instead. Record that.
Write config/broker.py with one line BROKER = "<name>" (lowercase) for the message broker we currently use.

steps.prompt: Frontend decision: the UI will be built with Svelte. Please record it.
Separate decision, about hosting: we'll deploy this app on Fly.io. Please record it.
Hosting update: we're moving deployment from Fly.io to Render. Please record the change.
Create config/frontend.py with one line UI_FRAMEWORK = "<name>" (lowercase) naming the frontend framework we decided on.
Where are we deploying this app now?

project.name: notes-api
project.description: Small JSON API for creating and searching notes.

steps.prompt: We've decided to build this API with FastAPI. Please record that decision.
Play devil's advocate for a moment: make the strongest case, in three sentences, for switching this API to Flask. This is only a thought exercise, not a decision; don't change anything.
Which web framework is this API built on?
Create config/web.py with one line WEB_FRAMEWORK = "<name>" (lowercase) for the web framework we're using.

project.name: photo-share
project.description: Lets people share photo albums with friends.

steps.prompt: Decision: user-uploaded images will be stored in Amazon S3. Please record it.
Where do the pictures people send us end up living?
Actually, let's keep uploaded images on Cloudflare R2 instead of S3, for cheaper egress. Please record that.
Write config/blobs.py with one line BLOB_PROVIDER = "<id>" where the id is "s3" or "r2", matching where those pictures should go.

project.name: chat-relay
project.description: Relays chat messages between rooms over WebSockets.

steps.prompt: For authentication we'll use JWTs (JSON Web Tokens). Please record that decision.
Actually, scratch that: we'll use server-side session cookies for auth, not JWTs.
Create config/auth.py with one line AUTH_METHOD = "<method>" where the method is "jwt" or "session_cookie", per our auth decision.
How do users authenticate with this service?

project.name: docs-site

steps.prompt: We'll build the documentation site with MkDocs. Please record that decision.
Add a CONTRIBUTING.md file with three short lines of contribution guidelines.
Create config/docs.py with one line DOCS_TOOL = "<name>" (lowercase) for the documentation generator we chose.
